headline: Hold — positive on gold as a risk hedge, record $1 billion cash balance, $350 million buyback, upgrade cycle underway as gold price rises
reasoning: Perseus has a record billion-dollar cash balance and has increased its buyback to $350 million. The gold price has been trending upward, forcing analyst upgrades, creating positive momentum. The stock is slightly cheap relative to consensus forecasts which tend to lag the gold price. It spits out a lot of cash. With property and travel facing headwinds, gold offers a safer parking spot with potential tailwinds from global economic uncertainty. The minimal 2% dividend yield is a small bonus — you don't buy resource companies for yield. Would not rush to sell.
quote: It spits out a lot of cash. It's got a record billion dollar cash balance. It has a buyback in place and I think it's actually increased the buyback by 150 million to now 350 million dollars. So this is a ride space, ride time company. Spitting out a bucket load of cash quite literally... I think you do need to own some gold. I would call this one a hold.

headline: Sell — can't control commodity price or earnings stability; if you must own a gold miner, Perseus is well-run at low end of cost curve, but better places to put money
reasoning: Team Invest's general framework excludes all miners because you cannot control the price received for assets, which undermines earnings moats and stability. Perseus does tick boxes for being at the lower half of the cost curve and having a strong management track record of delivery. However, the fundamental question is why own a gold miner at all. If your thesis is gold as a risk hedge against global economic disruption, owning a well-run miner is better than a poorly-run one, but the preference is still to avoid.
quote: The problem with all commodities businesses is you cannot control the price you receive for your assets. And I've spoke about before that from a team invest point of view, that effectively knocks out all miners from us because you don't have control over the moats of the business and you don't have control around the stability of earnings... if your thesis is that Donald Trump is gonna wreck the global economy so much that gold will be sexy again, and you don't believe that other miners are gonna pick up the slack in production, then owning a well-run miner is far better than owning a poorly run miner. So from that point of view, I can see the attraction to some people, but that's just a long-winded way of excusing why I'm a seller.
